entries.appliesTo: any person offering therapy or psychotherapy services to the public (including via Internet-based AI) and Maine-licensed mental/behavioral health professionals using AI for administrative or supplementary support

dutySources.disclosure-ui: Sec. 2, 32 MRSA §2113(3)(A) — 'The client or the client's legally authorized representative is informed in writing of the following: (1) That artificial intelligence will be used; (2) The specific purpose of the artificial intelligence tool or system that will be used'
dutySources.consent-workflow: Sec. 2, 32 MRSA §2113(3)(B) — 'The client or the client's legally authorized representative provides consent to the use of artificial intelligence.'
dutySources.human-review: Sec. 2, 32 MRSA §2113(4)(C) — 'A licensee may not allow artificial intelligence to: … Generate therapeutic recommendations or treatment plans without review and approval by the licensee.'

exposure.enforcer: unfair-trade-practices-act (Sec. 1 unlicensed AI therapy ban) + licensing-board-discipline (Secs. 2-8 licensee AI-use rules)

sources.aiTherapyRule: Sec. 1, 10 MRSA §1500-EE(2) — 'A person may not provide, advertise or otherwise offer therapy or psychotherapy services, including through the use of Internet-based artificial intelligence, to the public unless the therapy or psychotherapy services are provided by a licensed professional.'; Sec. 2, 32 MRSA §2113(4)(B) — 'A licensee may not allow artificial intelligence to: … Directly interact with clients in any form of therapeutic communication'
sources.consentRequired: Sec. 2, 32 MRSA §2113(3)(B) — 'The client or the client's legally authorized representative provides consent to the use of artificial intelligence.'
sources.scope: Sec. 1, 10 MRSA §1500-EE(1)(D) — '"Therapy or psychotherapy services" means services provided to diagnose, treat or address an individual's mental health or behavioral health through therapeutic communication.'
sources.enforcer: Sec. 1, 10 MRSA §1500-EE(3) — 'A violation of subsection 2 is a violation of the Maine Unfair Trade Practices Act.'; Sec. 2, 32 MRSA §2113(8) — 'A violation of this section is subject to disciplinary action by the board pursuant to Title 10, section 8003, subsection 5.'

flags: aiTherapyRule=ban is slightly lossy: AI may not provide therapeutic communication or make independent therapeutic decisions (§2113(4)), but licensees may use AI for administrative support and, with consent, supplementary support (§2113(2)-(3)) — a supervised carve-out for non-therapeutic tasks

Secs. 2-8 enact verbatim-identical AI-support regimes across seven Title 32 licensing chapters (§§2113, 2600-G, 3300-J, 3820-A, 6207-D, 7009, 13870) covering the mental/behavioral health licensed professions; coded once

Dual enforcement routes with no fine stated in this text: unlicensed-provision ban routed to the Maine Unfair Trade Practices Act (rule 4, no penaltyMax imported); licensee provisions routed to board discipline under Title 10 §8003(5)
Supplementary-support use additionally conditioned on session recording/transcription: §2113(3) — 'only when the client's therapeutic session is recorded or transcribed'

No listed duty fits: confidentiality-compliance mandate (§2113(6) — 'shall ensure that any artificial intelligence technology is compliant with all state and federal confidentiality and privacy laws'), denial-of-treatment prohibition (§2113(5) — 'may not deny, or refuse to provide, therapy or psychotherapy services … on the sole basis that the client has not provided consent'), client-waiver voidness (§2113(11)), and preserved private right of action for harm/negligence (§2113(12))
Exception: AI-based interventions 'used solely within a research project approved by an institutional review board' exempt (§1500-EE(4), §2113(9))
Boards must adopt implementing rules that are 'major substantive rules' (§2113(10)) — future rulemaking not coded
